pages.title: OpenVibe
pages.body:
The **OpenVibe network** is a set of services built in the open by OpenVibers, whose repositories are published in the [OpenVibers](https://github.com/OpenVibers) GitHub organisation. [[OpenVibe.Network]] is the network's identity and account service. This space describes the network's products as their README and STATUS files state them at the cited commits.

## Streaming and media

- [[OpenVibe.Live]] — the streaming front: ingest, viewer playback, channels, streamer tools and moderation.
- [[OpenVibe.Media]] — the multi-tenant media service for VODs, clips, files, thumbnails and storage tiering.
- [[OpenVibe.Zone]] — private S3-compatible storage zones for every project.
- [[OpenVibe.MediaHub]] — openvibe.download (a private drive), openvibe.video (uploads and AI edits) and openvibe.pics (pictures).
- [[OpenRestream]] — the ingest and restream control plane extracted from OpenVibe.Live.

## Community and content

- [[OpenVibe.Community]] — pastes, the forum, the comment threads other products embed, Pulse and submissions.
- [[OpenVibe.Blog]] — the official blog and a blog for every member.
- [[OpenVibe.News]] — editor-written, source-backed stories assembled from collected news items.
- [[OpenVibe.Reviews]] — review signals with provenance, entity resolution and honest aggregates.
- [[OpenVibe.Chat]] — the communication authority for rooms, messages, DMs, calls, TTS and moderation.
- [[OpenVibe.Space]] — a site for code, dynamic pages and spaces, still a home page today.
- [[OpenVibe.Help]] — the help and support centre generated from the product manifests.
- [[OpenVibe.Quest]] — one quest log across every OpenVibe site, awarding badges and OpenCoins.

## Tools and games

- [[OpenVibe.Tools]] — the tools suite: a tool registry, a run API, jobs and a shared guard.
- [[OpenVibe.Games]] — Scraplandia, a persistent multiplayer physics sandbox in the browser, and worlds players build and publish.
- [[OpenVibe.Play]] — achievements and leaderboards for every OpenVibe game.
- [[OpenVibe.Food]] — food near a place, a meal planner, a pantry, AI recipes, and delivery apps and meal kits compared.

## Developer platform

- [[OpenVibe.Network]] — identity, OAuth2 SSO, notifications and the OpenCoins wallet.
- [[OpenVibe.Events]] — the durable event backbone: delivery, retry, dead letters and replay.
- [[OpenVibe.Search]] — permission-aware discovery with an ACL-filtered query API.
- [[OpenVibe.Sources]] — the source registry and ingestion workers with recorded provenance.
- [[OpenVibe.Publishing]] — the shared publishing packages the publication products build on.
- [[OpenVibe.Wiki]] — this wiki: spaces, page trees, revisions, citations and discussion.
- [[OpenVibe.Codes]] — the open coding-agent harness.
- [[OpenVibe.Services]] — the developer console for projects, apps, credentials and grants.
- [[OpenVibe.Host]] — the deployment and control plane (the ovhost CLI) and tenant static hosting.
- [[OpenVibe.Run]] — the job service that places jobs on nodes and follows them to an end.

## Agents and automation

- [[OpenVibe.Actor]] — OpenVibe's own general agent and agent router.
- [[OpenVibe.Bot]] — the open control panel for robots.
- [[OpenVibe.Node]] — one service on your own computers and robots, used by Bot and Actor.
- [[OpenVibe.AI]] — the AI authority for providers, workflows, runs and quotas.
- [[OpenVibe.Watch]] — persistent, user-defined observations and conditions over pages, feeds and events.

## Commerce

- [[OpenVibe.Deals]] — community-submitted deals with observed prices and freshness.
- [[OpenVibe.Coupons]] — coupon codes with merchant matching and validity reports.
- [[OpenVibe.Trade]] — informational watchlists and sourced market context, with no order execution.
- [[OpenVibe.Rent]] — every rental site in one search, a board for listings from anywhere, and OpenVibe.Homes for buying.
- [[OpenVibe.Inventory]] — the network-wide inventory of items a person owns.
- [[OpenVibe.Work]] — job listings gathered from open job boards.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Network
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Network** is the identity and account service of the OpenVibe network, at `openvibe.network` on port 4000. Its README states that it manages "user accounts, OAuth2 authorization, theme preferences, notifications, email alerts, anonymous identities, the network-wide OpenCoins wallet, and internal APIs that connect all OpenVibe services together."

## What it does

It is the network's single sign-on provider, described as "One Account. All of OpenVibe." It runs an OAuth2 Authorization Code flow with PKCE for [[OpenVibe.Live]], [[OpenVibe.Tools]], [[OpenVibe.Games]] and [[OpenVibe.Media]], plus OpenID Connect discovery and an RS256 id_token. It issues RS256 access tokens and rotating refresh tokens stored only as a SHA-256. It owns accounts, anonymous identities, multi-account switching, the notification system with priority levels, email alerts, a theme catalog, an admin panel, an internal service-to-service API and the OpenCoins wallet. It also runs the service registry and public discovery, public profiles at `/@<username>`, the follow graph, platform blocks, creator analytics and developer projects.

## What it does not do yet

The README says it does not own money (that is OpenVibe.Billing) or channel points and streams ([[OpenVibe.Live]]). A notification digest "is designed ... for a later release."

## How it fits the network

Network is the token issuer, so other services verify its tokens offline. It publishes events to [[OpenVibe.Events]] through an outbox when `OV_EVENTS_INTERNAL_URL` is set, consumes Events deliveries for go-live notifications, and calls [[OpenVibe.AI]] for the footer's site copy. Its developer-project console is [[OpenVibe.Services]].

## Runtime and status

Node/Express on PostgreSQL. Its STATUS.json marks the stage "stable" and records it deployed, "Public at https://openvibe.network".

pages.title: OpenVibe.Live
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Live** is the streaming front of the OpenVibe network, on port 3000 at `openvibe.live`. Its README says it "takes a streamer's video in, plays it to viewers, and gives the channel its page, chat, clips and tools."

## What it does

Live owns streaming ingest and viewer playback: RTMP through `node-media-server` on ports 1935/9935 at `ingest.openvibe.live`, optional WebRTC through `mediasoup`, JSMPEG, and WHIP/HTTP ingestion on `whip.openvibe.live`. It owns channels and streams (go-live, stream keys, managed streams, heartbeats, channel pages at `/@username`), the watch experience, streamer tools (dashboard, restreaming, song requests, AI viewers), channel points, Vibes tipping flows, moderation, and the Arena (Battle Cam). Its local data lives in PostgreSQL `ov_live`.

## What it does not do yet

Identity, sessions, follows, blocks, notifications and OpenCoins belong to [[OpenVibe.Network]]. Chat and its messages belong to [[OpenVibe.Chat]] "since 2026-09-23"; Live dropped the twelve tables it still held. Recordings, clips, thumbnails and files belong to [[OpenVibe.Media]]; pastes and comments belong to [[OpenVibe.Community]]; AI belongs to [[OpenVibe.AI]], and the README says Live calls no model provider itself except for live-stream captions.

## How it fits the network

Live signs in through [[OpenVibe.Network]] as OAuth client `live` and verifies tokens offline. It depends on [[OpenVibe.Media]] for VOD recording and storage, and calls [[OpenVibe.Chat]], [[OpenVibe.Community]], [[OpenVibe.AI]], [[OpenVibe.Events]], [[OpenVibe.Tools]] and [[OpenVibe.Search]] with its service token.

## Status

Its STATUS.json marks the stage "stable" and records a production release layout under `/opt/openvibe.live`.
pages.summary: The streaming front of the OpenVibe network: ingest (RTMP, WHIP, WebRTC, JSMPEG), viewer playback, channels, the watch page, streamer tools, moderation and restreaming.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Media
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Media** is the standalone multi-tenant media service extracted from the OpenVibe.Live predecessor, at `openvibe.media` on port 4100. Its README states that it "Owns VOD ingest/recording, storage tiering (local → Backblaze B2 → Cloudflare R2), clips, generic files, the canonical object model and thumbnails, for all OpenVibe apps."

## What it does

Media records VODs from RTMP pull or RTP ingest, ingests browser chunks, finalizes with remux, probe and thumbnail, and cuts clips. It tiers storage across local, Backblaze B2 and Cloudflare R2 with copy verification and a disk guardian, and serves public paths (`/v`, `/c`, `/t`, `/f`, `/o`). It implements a canonical object model under `/api/v2` (objects, locations, variants, holds, derivatives, lifecycle, namespaces) and a media jobs queue. It serves first-party tenants (`live`, `community`, `tools`, `games`, `wiki`, `blog`, `inventory`, `media-hub`) and developer-project tenants.

## What it does not do yet

Pastes belong to [[OpenVibe.Community]] "since 2026-09-22"; Media's read-only paste API is gone and `/p/:slug` redirects there. Channels and streams belong to [[OpenVibe.Live]], identity to [[OpenVibe.Network]], and AI analysis of recordings to [[OpenVibe.AI]]. The song-request media queue, server-side live thumbnail grabbers and JSMPEG stdin recording are listed as "Not ported."

## How it fits the network

Media verifies [[OpenVibe.Network]] tokens offline through JWKS, uses [[OpenVibe.Live]]'s lineage resolve, and announces outcomes as [[OpenVibe.Events]] events through the SDK outbox, which the README calls the only outcome announcement now that webhooks ended.

## Status

Its STATUS.json marks the stage "beta" and records it deployed with `sudo ovhost deploy media`.
pages.summary: The multi-tenant media service: VOD ingest and recording, storage tiering across local, B2 and R2, clips, files, thumbnails and the canonical object model.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Community
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Community** is the community hub of the OpenVibe network, at `openvibe.community`. Its README describes it as the home of pastes, the forum, the typed comment threads every other OpenVibe product embeds, Pulse and submissions.

## What it does

Since 2026-09-22 Community is "the only paste authority", holding code, text and screenshots with versions, likes, comments and forks. It also runs the forum (spaces, threads, posts, votes and categories), the typed comment threads other products embed, Pulse (the network's public activity), submissions for community review, and a Discord relay. Every page is server-rendered so "crawlers and no-JS readers get the whole thing". It owns one PostgreSQL database, `ov_community`, with Valkey for per-actor limit counters.

## What it does not do yet

The README says comments, the forum and Pulse "are deployed but hold almost nothing yet", and that "the Discord relay is off". Community does not own identity and SSO, file bytes, memberships or chat rooms.

## How it fits the network

It depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO and JWKS, [[OpenVibe.Media]] for screenshot and attachment uploads, OpenVibe.VIP for members-only gates, [[OpenVibe.Chat]] for a space's chat room, and [[OpenVibe.Events]] for the outbox relay and subscriptions.

## Runtime and status

It is a small Node/Express app (CommonJS, no framework) over PostgreSQL, listening on `127.0.0.1:4200` behind nginx. STATUS.json records the stage as "alpha" and the service deployed with `sudo ovhost deploy community`.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Events
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Events** is the durable event backbone of the OpenVibe network, at `openvibe.events`. Its README describes it as "Durable events, subscriptions, delivery, retry, dead letters and replay for the network."

## What it does

Every authoritative service writes domain mutations and outbox events in one transaction, a relay publishes them to Events, consumers use inbox and idempotency receipts, and browsers get resumable projections through the Realtime delivery plane. It stores events, subscriptions, deliveries and checkpoints in PostgreSQL (`ov_events`), signs webhook deliveries with signature v2, retries with backoff, keeps a dead-letter queue and supports replay. It also serves developer apps with sandbox separation, per-project quotas and SSRF-guarded webhooks. Retention is tiered: hot, a replay tier (`events_archive`) and an operator-run monthly NDJSON archive.

## What it does not do yet

It does not own media bytes, game or media transport packets, or product business rules. WebSocket and presence are "not built yet". Carrier options such as NATS Core, JetStream and a cloud SQS-compatible queue are optional and off unless configured.

## How it fits the network

Live, Media, Chat, Games, Network and OpenRestream publish to it in production, and every consumer webhook requires signature v2. It is consumed by [[OpenVibe.Search]] and other services, and depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for token signing keys and subject ids. The README records that it "Replaces the best-effort internal POSTs/webhooks between Live, Media, Network and Community."

## Runtime and status

It runs on Node 22 and Express, listening on `127.0.0.1:4300` behind nginx. STATUS.json records the stage as "alpha" and the service deployed with `sudo ovhost deploy events`. License: AGPL-3.0.
pages.summary: The durable event backbone of the network: event storage, subscriptions, signed delivery, retry, dead letters, replay and realtime SSE.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Search
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Search** is the permission-aware discovery service of the OpenVibe network, at `search.openvibe.network`. Its README describes "the canonical index document, event-fed indexing" and "an ACL-filtered query API, and deletion/visibility propagation".

## What it does

Every publication product tells Search about its resources through one contract, `search.index-document@1`. Search answers queries "without ever returning a document the caller may not see". It provides a query API (`GET /api/v1/search`, `/api/v1/suggest`, `/api/v1/documents/:owner/:type/:id`), facets, freshness-weighted ranking, saved searches, and a server-rendered search page useful without JavaScript. It stores documents, ACLs, facets and a full-text index in PostgreSQL (`ov_search`), fed through [[OpenVibe.Events]]. A visibility change or deletion leaves results immediately and emits `search.document.removed`, which can also queue a Cloudflare CDN purge.

## What it does not do yet

Indexing works end to end in production: on 2026-10-14 Search held 10,438 documents that products had sent through [[OpenVibe.Events]]. No product polls the removal feed yet, and the CDN purge needs a Cloudflare token with Cache Purge permission. Search does not own any product's content, publication state or indexability decision, nor sitemaps, feeds or page caches.
## How it fits the network

Owners can write documents directly with an owner token or, preferably, publish index-document events through [[OpenVibe.Events]]. Search calls [[OpenVibe.Network]] for signing keys, and with saved-search notifications on it can resolve a subject and push a notification.

## Runtime and status

It runs on Node 22 and Express with PostgreSQL full-text search, listening on `127.0.0.1:4710` behind nginx. STATUS.json records the stage as "alpha" and the service deployed with `sudo ovhost deploy search`. License: AGPL-3.0.
pages.summary: The permission-aware discovery service: a canonical index document, event-fed indexing and an ACL-filtered query API.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Sources
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Sources** is the source registry and ingestion service of the OpenVibe network, at `sources.openvibe.network` on port 4720, with a loopback-only API. The README calls it "The source registry and the ingestion workers the publication products depend on."

## What it does

Sources owns the one place outside material enters the network: a registry of sources with their terms, plus workers that fetch them politely and record what happened. News, Reviews, Deals, Coupons, Trade and AI summarisation all read items with provenance from here. A source records its type (`rss|atom|sitemap|jsonld|api|manual`), category, endpoints, auth, robots and terms notes, rate limits and indexability. Adapters parse RSS, Atom, sitemaps, JSON-LD and official APIs. Every attempt writes a `fetch_runs` row with an explicit state, and the README states a failed fetch is a recorded failure, never replaced by invented content. Items keep revisions and provenance, and removal is explicit.

It also keeps what a deal feed states in its own elements: DealNews' price, currency, retailer and end date become item fields exactly as written (`feed@2`), so [[OpenVibe.Deals]] shows them without reading prices out of headlines.

## Sources today

On 2026-10-16, 35 of 39 sources were enabled, with 17,965 items from 2,156 fetch runs: 19 review sources, 4 market sources for Trade, 4 news wires, 3 hosting catalogues, 2 coupon feeds, and one each for blog desks, crowdfunding and deals.

## What it does not do

Sources does not decide what a product publishes. A person reads each source's robots and terms notes before enabling it, and a source whose robots file refuses the fetch stays disabled. It never calls [[OpenVibe.AI]].

## How it fits the network

Products are the only clients of both Sources and [[OpenVibe.AI]]: a product reads items and passes them to AI as run input. Sources emits `sources.item.*`, `sources.fetch.failed` and staff-only index documents through the [[OpenVibe.Events]] outbox, and raw items reach [[OpenVibe.Search]] for staff only, always `noindex`. It depends on [[OpenVibe.Host]] data roles, PostgreSQL and [[OpenVibe.Network]] signing keys.

## Runtime and status

Node 22 and Express on PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey 9, unit `openvibe-sources.service` on `127.0.0.1:4720`, database `ov_sources`. STATUS.json records the stage as "alpha" and the service deployed. License: AGPL-3.0.
pages.summary: The source registry and ingestion workers that fetch outside material with recorded provenance; 35 sources feed Deals, News, Reviews, Trade, Host, Coupons and Blog.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Publishing
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Publishing** is the shared publishing package library for the OpenVibe publication products: Wiki, Blog, News, Reviews, Deals, Coupons and Trade. Its README says it is "code, never state".

## What it provides

The package `openvibe-publishing` (CommonJS, Node 20 or later) gives the publication products one implementation of how they publish: immutable revisions with diff and revert, scheduling, taxonomy, citations, media and discussion references, the deterministic indexability gate, redirects, sitemaps and feeds, authorship and AI disclosure, Search documents, and server-rendered HTML. It also carries the shared ingest chassis (the [[OpenVibe.Sources]] client, a change cursor and a pull loop) and the publication glue. Each module is its own entry point, and each release is additive.

## What it does not do

This repository has no runtime, no port, no domain, no database and no API of its own, and the README states it must never get one. It owns no state: each product keeps its publication state in its own database, and the stores use prefixed tables inside that product's database. It does not decide editorial rules, store comment content, or act as a notification, search or event runtime.

## How it fits the network

All seven products pin a released tag; Wiki and Blog are public, while News, Reviews, Deals, Coupons and Trade are deployed loopback-only. Four modules call services with the product's own token: discussion calls [[OpenVibe.Community]], `ai` calls [[OpenVibe.AI]], media's verify reads [[OpenVibe.Media]], and ingest reads [[OpenVibe.Sources]]. It builds the documents and envelopes that [[OpenVibe.Search]] and [[OpenVibe.Events]] consume.

## Status

Alpha. The README states the current round is 1.3.0, while STATUS.json records 1.4.0. Nothing is deployed from this repository: a release is a git tag, and products pin the tag's tarball. License: MIT.
pages.summary: The shared publishing package library (openvibe-publishing) that gives the publication products revisions, the indexability gate, feeds and ingest glue; code only, with no runtime of its own.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Wiki
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Wiki** is the knowledge product of the OpenVibe network, public at `https://openvibe.wiki` since 2026-09-23 on port 4800 (service id `wiki`). It is alpha.

## What it does

Wiki offers spaces (official and user), page trees with canonical slugs, immutable revisions with diff and revert, manual editing without JavaScript, typed infoboxes, internal links, citations attached to the revision that used them, [[OpenVibe.Media]] attachments and [[OpenVibe.Community]] discussion. It supports public, members, VIP, private and members-only visibility. Its README calls it the first full consumer of the shared publishing packages ([[OpenVibe.Publishing]]): revisions, citations, redirects, the gate, feeds, sitemaps and Search hooks come from there, while Wiki owns its publication state.

## What it does not do yet

The official space's pages were revised on 2026-10-14 from each repository's README and STATUS. No person has reviewed them yet, so they stay `noindex`. Not built yet:

- page-level talk moderation;
- media upload from Wiki (it links existing objects only);
- consuming Media and Sources change events;
- per-space feeds and full-text ranking.

AI is a seam only: Wiki makes no AI provider calls, and a proposal waits for a person's approval.
## How it fits the network

Wiki depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO and identity, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for its outbox, [[OpenVibe.Community]] for threads, [[OpenVibe.Sources]] for citations, [[OpenVibe.Media]] for attachments, OpenVibe.VIP for VIP spaces, and [[OpenVibe.Search]] as the consumer of its index documents. [[OpenVibe.AI]] would file proposals, but the README says the API is not wired yet.

## Runtime and status

Node 22 and Express, PostgreSQL 18 (`ov_wiki`) and Valkey 9, unit `openvibe-wiki.service` on `127.0.0.1:4800`. Deployed and public. License: AGPL-3.0.
pages.summary: The wiki product of the network: spaces, page trees, immutable revisions, citations, infoboxes, internal links, media and discussion, public since 2026-09-23.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Codes
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Codes** is the open coding-agent harness of the OpenVibe network, public at `https://openvibe.codes` on port 4900 (service id `codes`). It is alpha.

## What it does

Codes is "the open coding-agent harness for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Command Code, Aider, the DeepSeek API and models you host yourself". The `openvibe-codes` command, a CLI and Node.js module, runs a coding task on an agent that fits it, hands the task to the next agent when one fails or goes quiet, and keeps every run. Every adapter turns its agent's output into one Claude Code `stream-json`-shaped event stream, with keys, tokens and private keys redacted. The site carries the agent catalog, a public routing API (`POST /api/v1/harnesses/route`), getting started, Improve OpenVibe and the community documents. Everything is server-rendered and usable without JavaScript.

## What it does not do yet

On 2026-10-08 the developer console that used to live here moved to [[OpenVibe.Services]], and every former console address answers a permanent redirect there. Codes is now the open coding-agent harness and its CLI. Not built yet:

- a hosted runner on [[OpenVibe.Run]] with budgets and metering, which waits for a separate isolated worker host;
- pushes to a person's own GitHub, which wait for a GitHub OAuth app;
- the community documents, which are drafts pending the owner's review.
## How it fits the network

Codes signs in with [[OpenVibe.Network]] and depends on PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey 9 on [[OpenVibe.Host]]. It does not own accounts, projects or grants ([[OpenVibe.Network]]) or provider keys ([[OpenVibe.AI]]). The harness runs on a person's own machine with their own CLIs and keys; nothing goes through OpenVibe.

## Runtime and status

Node 22 and Express 4, PostgreSQL 18 (`ov_codes`) and Valkey 9, unit `openvibe-codes.service` on `127.0.0.1:4900`. STATUS.json records the stage as "alpha" and the service deployed. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Services
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Services** is the developer platform of the OpenVibe network, serving `https://openvibe.services` on port 4930 (service id `services`). It is alpha. Its README describes it as "one console for projects and apps over OpenVibe.Network".

## What it does

It shows and forwards what the signed-in person asks for, with that person's own [[OpenVibe.Network]] token: projects, members, apps, credentials, capability grants and quotas; a per-project usage page from Network's rollups; project export as JSON and a full archive as a zip; OAuth and webhook tools that speak signature v2 only; and Media and Events playgrounds. Its merged resource index reads each authority with its own token and merges the pages, naming any authority it could not read.

It also sends control requests to the service that holds a resource, which decides:
- **project resources:** an admin can suspend, resume, stop or delete them (watches, event subscriptions, Actor tasks, Media objects, Space sites, Zone zones);
- **a person's own resources**, on "Your resources": they can stop or resume their robot, archive a chat room, suspend or resume a restream, and delete a paste.

Every request is idempotent and audited. An agent's sensitive request waits for its owner's approval. Secrets are shown once and never stored. Everything is server-rendered and usable without JavaScript.

## What it does not do yet

The developer portal moved here from [[OpenVibe.Codes]] on 2026-10-08, when its production data was nil, so nothing was copied. The playgrounds have never been used on production; the one end-to-end run used curl and is not a committed, repeatable check. Not built yet: Billing sandbox, Chat bot and Realtime playgrounds, a CLI and scaffolding, templates, and a third-party consent screen. Governance material is in drafts pending owner review.

## How it fits the network

Services depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for identity, projects and the registry; on [[OpenVibe.Events]] for the outbox relay and the Events playground; and on [[OpenVibe.Media]] for uploads and the archive. It never copies another authority's data, and it never fetches a URL a developer types.

pages.title: OpenVibe.AI
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.AI** is the reusable AI authority of the OpenVibe network, on `127.0.0.1:4700` and public at `https://ai.openvibe.services` since 2026-10-07 (unit `openvibe-ai.service`). It is alpha.

## What it does

The README describes it as owning "providers, models, routing, prompt templates, workflows, runs, citations, cache and quotas for every product". Products run registered, versioned workflows, and every run returns a draft and evidence package (structured output plus citations and provenance) attributed to a workflow, its version, a model and a run id, never to a person. Providers include a deterministic `stub`, any OpenAI-compatible API, the OpenAI Responses API, Anthropic, an HTTP seam, whisper.cpp and a local llama.cpp model. Routing can fall back, with circuit breakers; quotas refuse before any provider call; a person's own provider key is encrypted at rest. A staff operator console is server-rendered and needs [[OpenVibe.Network]] SSO.

## What it does not do yet

The README states that AI never owns publication truth: Wiki, Blog, News, Live and the rest decide what is published. Developer-app runs stay on local capacity while no tier budget governs their project, and metered models are not yet in use there. Live's VOD and clip overviews do not yet call `media.analyze`; speech and embedding routes still have a single upstream and answer `503 provider.unavailable` when it fails. `/metrics` is built but not deployed.

## How it fits the network

[[OpenVibe.Live]] runs with `AI_SERVICE=remote`, so its shared-key calls become runs here, and [[OpenVibe.Network]]'s footer copy calls `network.site_copy`. AI depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]], [[OpenVibe.Events]] for the `ai.run.*` outbox relay, [[OpenVibe.Media]] for recordings, and [[OpenVibe.Host]] data roles. Publishing products call AI's workflows for drafts; AI never publishes them.

## Runtime and status

Node 22 and Express on PostgreSQL (`ov_ai`); the local model runs as `openvibe-llm.service` on `127.0.0.1:8090`. STATUS.json records the stage as "alpha" and the service deployed. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.body:
**OpenRestream** is the ingest and restream control plane extracted from [[OpenVibe.Live]], served at `openre.stream` with RTMP ingest at `ingest.openre.stream`. A streamer goes live once from OBS or any RTMP encoder and can send the stream to Twitch, YouTube, Kick and other RTMP, RTMPS or SRT servers at the same time.

## What it does

The README states that OpenRestream owns stream definitions, ingest keys, ingest sessions, transport workers and their generations, restream destinations and outputs with health, recording requests to [[OpenVibe.Media]], and the `openre.*` lifecycle events. It states that RTMP ingest, restream, JSMPEG and WebRTC workers are ported and tested with real ffmpeg. The API and coordinator run on `127.0.0.1:4500`, and RTMP ingest is public on port 1936.

## What it does not do yet

`openre.stream` serves its own site since 2026-10-09, after an independent security review. Anyone signs in with OpenVibe, creates a stream with its RTMP key and sends it to other channels. A new stream also goes live on the person's [[OpenVibe.Live]] channel unless they untick that. No Live slot is ingested here yet: every slot is still ingested by Live until its own cutover. OAuth-linked destinations are not ported, and platform viewer counts, chat relay and PowerChat stay in Live.
## How it fits the network

It depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for JWKS and service tokens, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for event relay, [[OpenVibe.Media]] for recordings, and [[OpenVibe.Host]] for PostgreSQL and Valkey. [[OpenVibe.Live]] keeps the creator and channel product and observes sessions through OpenRestream APIs and events.

## Status

The README states the status is alpha (roadmap Wave 7), tested end to end with real RTMP; the site is public since 2026-10-09. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Watch
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Watch** is a service for persistent, user-defined observations and conditions over pages, feeds, APIs, webhooks and OpenVibe events, served at `openvibe.watch`. A person or an agent defines what to watch and is told when it changes or fires.

## What it does

The README states that the registry, the check engine, the pull carriers and the public site exist. The `http`, `feed` and `api` carriers are implemented, plus `event` and `webhook` sources. Every page of the public site is server-rendered and complete without JavaScript, with sign-in through [[OpenVibe.Network]] using OAuth 2 with PKCE (S256). A check uses a conditional GET, so it never polls when an ETag or an event will do, and the API is loopback-only.

## What it does not do yet

The README states that the event, webhook, Node and Run rungs and the actions do not yet work in full: a `run` source (browser or code polling through [[OpenVibe.Run]]) and a `node` probe are later steps, and a kind without a carrier is accepted but never fetched. The site offers only page, price, feed and JSON watches; the `ai` extraction is not a check.

## How it fits the network

Watch depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for signing keys and notifications, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for outbound events, and PostgreSQL 18. It does not own structured source ingestion (that is [[OpenVibe.Sources]]), expensive execution ([[OpenVibe.Run]]) or local probes.

## Status

The README states the status is alpha (plan T18 steps 2-3 and step 8). STATUS.json says the public site has been live since 2026-10-08 and that on 2026-10-10 it held no watches yet, so no check has run against a real site in production. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.MediaHub
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.MediaHub** is the network's file and media service. One process serves three sites, chosen by Host header, with every byte in [[OpenVibe.Media]].

## What it does

- **openvibe.download**, a private drive: a signed-in person uploads, organises, shares and deletes their own files (up to 25 GB each). Share links expire in one hour to seven days, are revocable and count downloads. **Sync keys** and the `openvibe-download` command keep a folder backed up, sending only what changed.
- **openvibe.video**: people upload videos or record them in the browser; [[OpenVibe.AI]] adds captions, chapters and a summary on OpenVibe's own servers, and the **AI cut** makes an edited copy with the pauses taken out, or a highlights reel. It also serves the watch pages and playlists for [[OpenVibe.Live]]'s stream recordings and clips, and public uploads are in [[OpenVibe.Search]].
- **openvibe.pics**: picture hosting with links to share and embed, albums, reports and takedown. Every picture is re-encoded with its location and camera details removed, comes in other sizes and formats (WebP, AVIF, JPEG, PNG), and carries alt text the uploader writes or asks AI to draft.

## What it does not do yet

Signed-out uploads on Pics and Download are built and switched off until the DMCA designated agent and the child-safety hash matching are in place.

## How it fits the network

MediaHub depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO and subject resolution, [[OpenVibe.Media]] for the bytes, [[OpenVibe.AI]] for the video edit and alt text, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for account export and deletion, and PostgreSQL and Valkey.

## Runtime and status

Port 4990, service id `media-hub`, status alpha; openvibe.download is public since 2026-10-08. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Blog
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Blog** hosts the official OpenVibe blog and a blog for every member, served at `openvibe.blog`. It provides drafts, revisions, series, scheduling and feeds.

## What it does

The README states the official blog exists from the first boot, and every member gets a blog on first use. Posts have drafts and immutable revisions with optimistic concurrency, diff and revert. Publishing, unpublishing, soft delete and scheduled publish or unpublish are supported. Tags, nested categories and ordered series organise posts, and slug changes leave 301s. Posts can use [[OpenVibe.Media]] for covers and figures, [[OpenVibe.Community]] for comment threads, and OpenVibe.VIP for members-only posts. A network changelog publishes Patch notes posts on the official blog. Pages are server-rendered and useful without JavaScript.

## What it does not do yet

The official blog is live. On 2026-10-14 it held 60 published posts, most of them Patch notes from the network changelog. The editor attaches existing `med_...` ids and does not upload. Media publishes no deletion event yet, so broken assets are found by polling. The Community thread visibility sync is best effort.
## How it fits the network

Blog depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO and subjects, [[OpenVibe.Media]] for attachments, [[OpenVibe.Community]] for comments, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for events and [[OpenVibe.Search]] for indexing.

## Status

The README states the status is alpha (roadmap Wave 16, Blog half), public at https://openvibe.blog since 2026-09-23. STATUS.json says it is deployed and that its capabilities and service manifest are registered. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.News
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.News** is a publication product, served at `openvibe.news`, that turns collected news items into editor-written, source-backed stories. The README calls it "A publication product, not an autonomous headline generator".

## What it does

[[OpenVibe.Sources]] collects news items, and News normalises them, removes duplicates, groups them into explainable clusters, and gives editors tools to write stories. Every paragraph an editor publishes cites the source items it rests on, and the README states a story with no sources cannot be published. Stories have immutable revisions, timelines, editor-written perspectives, corrections, updates and final retractions. Ingestion works two ways: an Events webhook and a cursor pull. Discussion threads are referenced from [[OpenVibe.Community]], and optional [[OpenVibe.AI]] drafts need a person's review. Pages are server-rendered and useful without JavaScript.

## What it does not do yet

The home page shows the latest items from the source wires, each linking to its source. Full article text from sources is never stored, shown, fed or indexed. Edited stories exist only once an editor opens one from a cluster and publishes it, and none has been published yet.
## How it fits the network

News depends on [[OpenVibe.Sources]] for items, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for events, [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO and subjects, [[OpenVibe.Community]] for comments and [[OpenVibe.Search]] for indexing.

## Status

The README states the status is alpha (roadmap Wave 17, News half), public at `openvibe.news` since 2026-10-09, and that STATUS.json records it deployed. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Reviews
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Reviews** is the interpretation and publication layer for review signals, served at `openvibe.reviews`. It reads what sources stated through [[OpenVibe.Sources]], attributes each observation to the thing it is about, and shows every number with its provenance.

## What it does

The README states Reviews resolves entities and computes an aggregate only from the signals that exist; with no qualifying signal the aggregate is absent, not zero. Signals arrive by a cursor pull and a signed webhook. Resolution is deterministic, strongest rule first, and a name alone never resolves. Merges and splits are audited and reversible. Summaries are written or approved by a person, and each point cites the signals it rests on. Corrections become new immutable summary revisions with a public notice. Pages and the editor desk are server-rendered and useful without JavaScript.

## What it does not do yet

Reviews never fabricates a rating and never presents AI output as user reviews. On 2026-10-14 it held 19 entities, Steam games whose review signals come from a Steam source in [[OpenVibe.Sources]]. Summaries written or approved by a person are still to come.
## How it fits the network

Reviews depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO and service principals, [[OpenVibe.Sources]] for review items, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for events and [[OpenVibe.Community]] for discussion threads.

## Status

The README states the status is alpha (roadmap Wave 17, Reviews half), public at `openvibe.reviews` since 2026-10-09, and that STATUS.json records it deployed, with none seeded. License: AGPL-3.0.

**OpenVibe.Help** is the help and support centre for every OpenVibe site, the service behind `openvibe.help` on port 5020 (service id `help`). Its README says "the product is written and tested; it is not deployed yet".

## What it does

At boot it reads the pinned OpenVibe.Contracts product and service manifests, builds a catalog of every site, and generates one article per manifest FAQ entry, quoting every text verbatim. `/search` ranks those articles with a fixed, explainable score and adds a second section from [[OpenVibe.Search]]'s public API, cached for five minutes and degrading to the articles alone on failure. A signed-in person opens a support ticket with a site, subject, message and an optional page URL stored as text and never fetched, and the ticket stays one conversation; staff are decided by the Network role claim.

## What it does not do yet

Help is live at `openvibe.help` since 2026-10-08, with its capabilities registered in the network's contracts. Not built yet:

- an email side to a ticket;
- a "Report a problem" button embedded on other OpenVibe sites;
- answers drawn from the docs, wiki, blog or service status.
## How it fits the network

It uses [[OpenVibe.Network]] for sign-in, JWKS and the role claim, [[OpenVibe.Search]] for the network half of `/search`, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for the two account export and deletion topics, and [[OpenVibe.Host]] for deploy, PostgreSQL and Valkey.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Food
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Food** answers "what should we eat?" for a household, served at `openvibe.food` on port 4970 (service id `food`).

## What it does

- **Food near you** (`/near`): food banks, soup kitchens, community fridges, community pantry boxes and budget grocery stores around a place, from OpenStreetMap, with distance, address and opening hours.
- **Meal planner** (`/plan`): a deterministic shop for one person, a couple or a group over one to fourteen days, one item from each of the six USDA MyPlate groups, with a shopping list, the cheapest store per line and a budget as a hard cap. A saved plan can be shared with a household, which ticks off one shopping list together.
- **Food database** (`/foods`): 42 items with nutrition and typical price bands.
- **Pantry** (`/pantry`): what is in the cupboard and which basic recipes it makes. Items go in by hand, by **barcode** (Open Food Facts names the product) or from a **photo of a shelf or a receipt** read by [[OpenVibe.AI]], always confirmed by the person.
- **Recipe ideas** (`/recipes`) from the pantry, and a **recipe library** (`/recipes/library`) written by AI from the food list, labelled as such and indexed only once staff have checked a recipe.
- **Delivery, compared** (`/delivery`): one search opens DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub, Seamless, Caviar and Instacart in new tabs, and meal kits and prepared meals (HelloFresh, Home Chef, EveryPlate, Factor and others) are listed by tier with their plans pages and an [[OpenVibe.Watch]] link for price changes.

Everything is server-rendered and works without JavaScript.

## What it does not do

Food fetches no delivery app's or meal kit's prices itself: their terms forbid automated collection, so it opens their own searches and pages for the person. Cost bands are typical carried-over values, not live figures.

## How it fits the network

It uses [[OpenVibe.Network]] for sign-in, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for the account topics, [[OpenVibe.AI]] for recipe ideas and pantry photos, [[OpenVibe.Search]] for checked recipes and [[OpenVibe.Host]] for deploy. A weekly budget-recipes desk on [[OpenVibe.Blog]] reads its library.

## Status

STATUS.json's stage is "product"; it is public since 2026-10-08. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Games** runs browser games at `openvibe.games` and `play.openvibe.games`, all from one TypeScript codebase with an authoritative server.

## What it does

- **Scraplandia** is a persistent multiplayer physics sandbox. Players gather in the wilds outside Scrap City, craft tools and building pieces, place them with a GMod-style physgun, and extract valuables in its scored "Haul" mode.
- **Salvage Rush** is a separate place in the same process: 90-second rounds of collecting scrap, scored by the server.
- **Vibe Heroes** (`/play/vibe-heroes`) is the first casual game: a phone-first idle hero collector built from a shared casual kit.
- **The client** runs Babylon.js, using WebGPU where the browser has it. Its quality tiers scale resolution, shadows and texture size on weak phones.
- **The server** keeps characters, inventories and the world in PostgreSQL, with deterministic Rapier physics.
- **Mods** add content packs and sandboxed script mods with per-mod capability grants.
- **The map editor** works in the browser and is tested end to end in CI.
- **Creator worlds** (`/worlds`): players build their own worlds in the map editor and publish them for anyone to join from the browser. They are sandboxes (characters are not saved there), run on demand, have their own pages and are in [[OpenVibe.Search]].

## How it fits the network

Players are keyed by [[OpenVibe.Network]] subjects.

- **Play.** Games registers Scraplandia and Salvage Rush as titles on [[OpenVibe.Play]] and posts every round, haul, achievement unlock and guest adoption there.
- **Inventory.** Some achievements grant cosmetic items through [[OpenVibe.Inventory]].
- **Events and Media.** Games publishes `games.*` events through [[OpenVibe.Events]] and mirrors map-editor assets to [[OpenVibe.Media]].

It deploys through [[OpenVibe.Host]].

pages.title: OpenVibe.Run
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Run** is the job service of the network, served at `openvibe.run` on port 4920. It accepts jobs, places each one on a node that advertises the runtime class it needs, and follows it to its end.

## What it does

A job belongs to a project, is billed per wall-clock second it runs, and is visible only to the token that project presents. Submit (`POST /api/v1/jobs`, capability `run.job.submit`) validates against a released contract, mints a `job_<ULID>` id, stores the row queued and writes `run.job.queued` in the same transaction. A poller places the job from the Fabric's offers using `openvibe-sdk/placement`, sends it to [[OpenVibe.Bot]], mirrors Bot's state and the node's stdout back, and settles it. `/api/v1/jobs/:id/stream` replays and follows a job's output as a server-sent event stream.

## What it does not do yet

Run serves its own site at `openvibe.run` since 2026-10-11. First-party callers such as [[OpenVibe.Codes]] submit jobs on loopback. A hosted runner for untrusted code waits for a separate, isolated worker host.
## How it fits the network

It verifies tokens issued by [[OpenVibe.Network]] and publishes `run.job.*` events to [[OpenVibe.Events]]. It owns no node link or per-second metering, which belong to [[OpenVibe.Bot]], and it holds no Billing token.

## Status

STATUS.json's stage is "alpha"; it is deployed on the host since 2026-10-07, with the job API reached by first-party callers on loopback.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Host
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Host** is two things. At `openvibe.host` it is **hosting compared**: a sourced comparison of cloud, VPS and dedicated plans, the offers providers post, and domain prices. Behind it is the network's deployment plane, the `ovhost` CLI, which deploys every OpenVibe service.

## Hosting plans

The README calls the catalog plan T20 step 3: "openvibe.host is **hosting compared**". Plans come from providers' official APIs through [[OpenVibe.Sources]] (category `hosting`) and from staff entries that must name their source URL. Each plan shows its monthly price, its price per vCPU and per GB of RAM and disk, the day the price was checked and a link to its source; price changes are kept as a history per plan, and [[OpenVibe.Watch]] can tell a visitor when a price changes. The order comes only from the sort a visitor picks, and affiliate links are marked with `rel="sponsored nofollow noopener"` and disclosed beside the link.

## Offers

`/catalog/offers` lists what providers post on LowEndTalk's Offers board and LowEndBox, read from their public feeds through Sources: the headline, who posted it, the date and the price the headline states, with its monthly equivalent. Each links to its post, which has the final word.

## Domains

`/catalog/domains` compares what registrars charge for each ending: the first year, a renewal, a transfer and the total over five years (the first year and four renewals at one registrar), with a mark where the renewal is more than a fifth above the first year. Prices come from registrars' public price lists through Sources, Porkbun's first. Each ending has its own page with every registrar's price and its change history. A name check asks the ending's registry over RDAP, the public lookup that replaced WHOIS: it says whether the name is registered (and through which registrar, since when and until when), prices the same name at popular endings, and links to the search at ten registrars.

## The deployment plane

The `ovhost` CLI holds the host inventory, validates environments, installs and rolls back releases, polls `/api/ready`, runs scheduled PostgreSQL backups and restore drills, and installs nginx vhosts transactionally. It is installed on the production host and deploys every service.

## What it does not do

Static site hosting moved to [[OpenVibe.Space]]; `*.openvibe.host` answers with a pointer there. Sandboxed user code (Stage C) is not started.

## How it fits the network

It uses [[OpenVibe.Network]] for sign-in and tokens, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for `host.*` events, [[OpenVibe.Sources]] for prices and offers, and [[OpenVibe.Search]] for its plan and provider pages; plan and provider pages have discussion threads on [[OpenVibe.Community]].

## Status

STATUS.json's stage is "alpha". License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Actor
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Actor** is OpenVibe's own general agent and the router for agent work, public at `openvibe.actor` on port 4950. It takes a task in plain words, sends it to the best agent system for it, streams the steps, has a model of another family check the answer, and gives back the result with its cost and the reason it went where it did.

## What it does

A task runs in five steps: classify it, route it with `openvibe-sdk/placement` over the agent catalog, run it while steps stream as events, check it with a model of another family, then deliver it or hand it on. Modes are cheapest, balanced, best, fastest and private. The OpenVibe runtime acts only through OpenVibe's public APIs: [[OpenVibe.Search]] content, [[OpenVibe.Tools]]' catalog and run API, and the Tools page reader. Private mode runs the open model on OpenVibe's own server, and the README says the task text never leaves OpenVibe. The API covers tasks, live server-sent events, cancel, a route dry run and personal agents.

## What it does not do yet

Since the first release, Actor has added:

- an approval inbox for the steps a person must confirm;
- signed webhooks on task state changes;
- computer control on a person's own machine through [[OpenVibe.Node]]: reading the screen and, at the level the person allows, the mouse and keyboard.

Coding tasks need [[OpenVibe.Run]] sandboxes and stay unavailable until an isolated worker host exists. A project secret named by reference is refused until project secrets exist. Paid tiers come later.
## How it fits the network

Actor depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for sign-in and tokens, [[OpenVibe.Search]] and [[OpenVibe.Tools]] at runtime, and [[OpenVibe.Events]] for its two boot-time subscriptions. It calls the model providers DeepSeek and OpenAI, plus an OpenAI-compatible local server for private mode. [[OpenVibe.Services]] reads its resource index over loopback.

## Status

Node 22 with Express, PostgreSQL for tasks, event logs and daily spend, and Valkey for shared limit counters. STATUS.json records it deployed; its stage is alpha. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Bot
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Bot** is "The open control panel for robots" at `openvibe.bot` on port 4630. It pairs a robot's machines, keeps their state and gates every operator command: a device opens one outbound WebSocket to `/device`, and a person drives it from `/control` or the REST API through the same gate of roles, per-robot limits, cooldowns and the turn budget.

## What it does

Bot owns robots, their profiles, per-robot limits, allow lists, roles and operators; the curated kit catalogue; devices and their hashed credentials; pairing codes; the `/device` and `/control` WebSockets, the command gate and the latched e-stop; and a command audit kept 30 days. A `sim.rover` robot is driven by an in-process simulator so the panel works before hardware exists, and server-side ONVIF cameras attach in-process. The panel renders from the robot's profile, with a touch joystick, keyboard and gamepad, a latency meter and one camera tile per camera. Owner-only streaming and recording toggles record live sessions to [[OpenVibe.Media]] or mirror them to the owner's [[OpenVibe.Live]] channel.

## What it does not do yet

Bot does not own identity, which is [[OpenVibe.Network]]'s, or video: a device publishes over WHIP to [[OpenRestream]]. When OpenVibe.Billing is unset, job usage readings wait in `run_usage_outbox` rather than being dropped.

## How it fits the network

Bot depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for user and service tokens, node tokens and identity resolution, [[OpenRestream]] for the WHIP ingest base devices publish to, and OpenVibe.Billing for job usage readings. A device's installer command points at the released OpenVibe.Node script.

## Status

Production runs the Node process under systemd as `openvibe-bot.service` on port 4630 behind nginx, which terminates TLS and upgrades the WebSockets. PostgreSQL applies `migrations/` at boot; Valkey is optional for shared per-actor limit counters. STATUS.json records stage alpha and the service deployed.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Chat
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Chat** is "The communication authority extracted from OpenVibe.Live": rooms, messages, DMs, calls, TTS and audio queues, moderation and presence, at `openvibe.chat` on port 4400. Since the cutover on 2026-09-23, Chat is the authority for openvibe.live's chat in every mode, and Live runs no chat of its own.

## What it does

Chat moved Live's WebSocket chat server, DMs, chat history, TTS, soundboards, moderation and word filter behind a service boundary. The TTS and sound queue persists requests in `audio_requests`, played one at a time per room and surviving a Chat restart. Chat owns its own PostgreSQL tables for messages, DMs, channel sounds, relay users and moderation actions, plus the six chat tables (moderators, moderation settings, emotes, tags, AI summaries, timeline). openvibe.chat adds public and private rooms with roles, the DM inbox, settings and calls. Member badges come from OpenVibe.VIP, chat-AI summaries run through [[OpenVibe.AI]], and emote image bytes live in [[OpenVibe.Media]].

## What it does not do yet

Live's voice and video calls are ported but not switched over yet (`CHAT_CALLS=1`). Chat produces no mention notifications; the @mention highlight is drawn by Live's chat client. Bans, channel moderation settings and the media-request queue are still Live's, reached through `live-context`.

## How it fits the network

Chat depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for identity and the `chat.preferences` user module, [[OpenVibe.Live]] until the rest of chat's data moves, [[OpenVibe.Events]], [[OpenVibe.Media]], OpenVibe.VIP and OpenVibe.Contracts. It is also served on openvibe.live's origin through an nginx include.

## Status

Node 22 with Express and ws, PostgreSQL through `openvibe-sdk/db`, and Valkey for per-actor limits. It is deployed as `openvibe-chat.service` on `127.0.0.1:4400`. Its stage is alpha. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Trade
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Trade** is an informational product at `openvibe.trade` on port 4860: instruments with deterministic resolution, sourced market observations, filings from [[OpenVibe.Sources]], private watchlists, alert rules and editor-written context. Its stated scope is "Informational watchlists, sourced market context and alerts. No custody, no order execution."

## What it does

Trade owns nine charter tables in its own PostgreSQL database, including immutable market observations and alert deliveries. Resolution is exact and deterministic (CIK, ticker, normalised name), with no fuzzy or prefix matching. Observations carry required `observed_at` and `retrieved_at` timestamps and show their source; where no observation exists the page says no number is shown. Per-source freshness renders a "stale since <time>" badge, and alerts fire on a crossing or a newly seen document, once per trigger. Editors publish cited context; [[OpenVibe.AI]] output is a labelled draft that cannot be published before a person on the editor list approves it, and advice is refused.

## What it does not do yet

The scope is informational only: there is no custody, no order execution, no escrow and no listing between users. No market data feed is configured, since the one seeded Sources trade source is disabled and carries filings, not prices, so a fresh deployment holds no instruments and no numbers at all until a source states values. Network notifications for `trade.alert.triggered` are not built yet.

## How it fits the network

Trade depends on [[OpenVibe.Sources]] for items, [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO and subjects, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for events, [[OpenVibe.Search]] for index documents and [[OpenVibe.AI]] for drafts.

## Status

Node 22, Express 4, PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey 9. It is public at its domain since 2026-10-09, after a pre-launch security review; `/api/ready` reports `degraded` because there is no feed. Its stage is alpha (roadmap Wave 19). License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Work
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Work** is the network's job-listings service at `openvibe.work` on port 4960. It gathers listings from public job boards, keeps each one's provenance and a short plain-text excerpt, and makes them searchable without an account.

## What it does

Work reads three boards, Arbeitnow, Remotive and RemoteOK, through their public APIs, on the terms each publishes, naming the source and linking back on every page. Its own PostgreSQL tables `work_listings`, `work_saved_searches` and `work_source_fetches` hold one row per listing (upserted on source and source id), saved searches and fetch records. Only a short excerpt, the README says "never the full description", is kept, and listings expire after 30 days unseen. Search has facets, a cursor and 30 per page, and one listing carries a `JobPosting` JSON-LD whose url is the original. A signed-in person can keep a search and see a `new_count` of what appeared since they last looked.

## What it does not do yet

The README's status says the agent pillar, "help preparing and tracking an application", is not written yet. Alerts are not built; they would come through [[OpenVibe.Watch]] with the agent pillar. The service manifest lists no capabilities, so app and agent tokens cannot call the person-only saved-search routes.

## How it fits the network

Work depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for SSO sign-in and JWKS verification, and on [[OpenVibe.Events]] for the two account subscriptions it creates at boot. It fetches only the three boards' public APIs and holds only person subjects on its own rows.

## Status

Node 22, Express 4, PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey 9. The ingest is off unless `WORK_INGEST=on`. It is deployed as `openvibe-work.service` on `127.0.0.1:4960`; STATUS.json records it public at https://openvibe.work since 2026-10-08 with stage "beta". License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Quest
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Quest** is "One quest log across every OpenVibe site" at `openvibe.quest` on port 4980. A quest counts something a person really did somewhere in the network and pays a badge on their profile; when OpenCoins are on, it also credits OpenCoins through [[OpenVibe.Network]]'s wallet.

## What it does

The quest catalog holds 12 first-party quests in code, each with steps, the events that count them, a badge, OpenCoins and any item reward, plus the whole list of events Quest listens to. Quest runs no activities of its own: it consumes domain events from [[OpenVibe.Events]] at `POST /internal/events`, taking the person from the field each event's schema defines. Progress is stored per step, with one completion per person per quest and one badge per person, all once-only under a redelivery. Six quests grant one of [[OpenVibe.Live]]'s items through [[OpenVibe.Inventory]]. The API exposes the catalog, a quest, your own log and a badges endpoint; the pages are server-rendered.

## What it does not do yet

Quest is deployed and public since 2026-10-08. OpenCoins are off until the feature is turned on (`QUEST_COINS`, default `off`). Community-made quests, leaderboards and repeatable quests are not implemented.
## How it fits the network

Quest depends on [[OpenVibe.Network]] for sign-in and crediting coins, [[OpenVibe.Events]] for deliveries, and [[OpenVibe.Inventory]] for item rewards. It counts events from [[OpenVibe.Live]], [[OpenVibe.Community]], [[OpenVibe.Space]], [[OpenVibe.Chat]], [[OpenVibe.Wiki]], [[OpenVibe.Games]] and [[OpenVibe.Tools]].

## Status

Node 22, Express 4, PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey 9. The README calls it a "first release". License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Deals
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Deals** is the network's deals site at `openvibe.deals`, in the spirit of Slickdeals: people post and vote on deals, and deals are imported from permitted feeds, each with its source, price and freshness shown.

## What it does

It keeps offers with timestamped price, shipping, condition and availability observations. A price is an observation: each has a source and an `observed_at` time, is shown "as of" that time, and is never presented as current without a fresh observation. Deals imported from DealNews through [[OpenVibe.Sources]] carry the price, the retailer and the end date the feed states: the retailer is the offer's seller ("at Amazon"), while the link goes to DealNews' own page, credited on every card. On 2026-10-16 there were 2,067 imported offers. Imported deals are noindex until a person reviews them, and DealNews' deals are kept out of browser extensions, as its feed terms require.

Votes and hotness (`hot@1`) are server-authoritative and deterministic. It has duplicate merge and unmerge, watches and saved searches (a match reaches the person's OpenVibe inbox through [[OpenVibe.Network]]), moderation and abuse controls, a crowdfunding search across Kickstarter, Indiegogo and other platforms, and server-rendered pages, feeds and sitemaps useful without JavaScript.

## What it does not do

It never invents a price or fills in a missing one: a deal whose source states no price says so. It imports only from sources whose terms were checked.

## How it fits the network

Discussion is [[OpenVibe.Community]]'s; imports come from [[OpenVibe.Sources]]; watch matches are delivered by [[OpenVibe.Network]]. It publishes through [[OpenVibe.Events]] and emits [[OpenVibe.Search]] documents. Coupon codes are [[OpenVibe.Coupons]]'.

## Status

It runs on Node 22 and Express with PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey 9, on port 4840. It is licensed AGPL-3.0.

**OpenVibe.Coupons** is the network's coupon service: codes with merchant matching, restrictions, expiry and real-people validity reports. It has been public at openvibe.coupons since 2026-10-09.

## What it does

Coupons keeps merchants and their normalized domains, codes, restrictions, validity reports, expiry and confidence. Four rules shape it, per the README: no code is labelled working because a model guessed it; unknown stays unknown; expired codes leave active results at the instant of expiry; and a merchant page cannot obtain anyone's data. It provides the public API that the OpenVibe Companion browser extension uses (described at openvibe.coupons/companion: codes for the shop you are on, tried in its coupon box when you ask, never rewriting referral links), server-rendered pages useful without JavaScript, feeds and sitemaps, and a confidence formula computed only from recent reports by people.

## What it does not do yet

A code's status comes only from recent reports, evidence or its source, never from a model's guess. On 2026-10-14 production held 16 codes, published automatically from the DealNews source in [[OpenVibe.Sources]] across 37 merchants. There is no Community discussion on code pages yet, and no staff UI to edit a code's text or restrictions.
## How it fits the network

Deal offers belong to [[OpenVibe.Deals]]; discussion belongs to [[OpenVibe.Community]]; identity and the notification store are [[OpenVibe.Network]]'s; [[OpenVibe.Search]] indexes what Coupons sends through [[OpenVibe.Events]]; ingestion belongs to [[OpenVibe.Sources]].

## Status

It runs on Node 22 and Express with PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey 9, on port 4850. It is licensed AGPL-3.0.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Rent
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Rent** is the network's rental aggregator at `openvibe.rent`: every rental site, one search. It covers apartments, rooms, houses, furnished stays, commercial space, parking, storage and cars.

## What it does

- **Search everywhere** (`/everywhere`): one place and one set of filters open each site's own search there, with price and bedroom filters where the site takes them: Craigslist, Facebook Marketplace, Zillow, Apartments.com, Zumper, Rent.com, RentCafe, Apartment List, PadMapper, HotPads, Trulia and Realtor.com for homes; Roomies and Furnished Finder for rooms; LoopNet for commercial space; SpotHero for parking; SpareFoot for storage; Turo for cars. The listings, messages and payments stay on each site, in the person's own browser and account.
- **The board** (`/board`): listings from any site in one OpenVibe list, with notes and how far the person got. The OpenVibe Companion browser extension keeps a listing on the board from the page the person is on.
- **Rent by city** (`/in`): a page for 885 US cities with the typical rent by number of bedrooms from the Census Bureau's American Community Survey, every rental site's search for that city, affordable housing and nearby cities; each is also an [[OpenVibe.Search]] document. **Is this rent fair?** (`/fair`) compares any quoted rent with the city's median; the Companion's "Check the rent" opens it from a listing on any site, and Rent says what it read from the listing.
- **Listings posted here** by people, searchable, with reports, renewals and 30-day expiry; never a street address, and no payments, deposits or messaging.
- **Affordable housing near you** (`/housing`): public housing, tax-credit and HUD-assisted properties, housing authorities and counselling agencies near a place, from HUD's public-domain data, with the FHFA home-price index beside them.
- **OpenVibe.Homes** (`openvibe.homes`), the buying side served by the same process: for-sale sites, government and bank homes, land and commercial property, county records and a mortgage calculator.

## How it aggregates

Sites whose terms forbid automated collection are combined the permitted way: deep links into each site's own search, the browser extension inside the person's own sessions, licensed feeds, and people posting. Licensed listing feeds through [[OpenVibe.Sources]] come next. The United States comes first; elsewhere a place gets the sites that work worldwide.

## How it fits the network

Accounts come from [[OpenVibe.Network]]; saved searches alert through [[OpenVibe.Watch]]; listings are screened for scam signs by [[OpenVibe.AI]] for staff, and its pages are in [[OpenVibe.Search]].

## Status

It runs on Node 22 with PostgreSQL and Valkey, on port 5010, public since 2026-10-08. License: AGPL-3.0.

pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Inventory** is the network-wide inventory for an OpenVibe account (ADR-054): your items, on every OpenVibe site. It is at the alpha stage (plan track T21 step 2), and its authority, API, pages and Live's migration script are built and tested.

## What it does

Inventory holds the items people earn or are given across every site, game and app. It registers item kinds (a contract plus a renderer per surface), the definitions an issuer publishes and the instances a person owns, and keeps what each person has equipped. Every movement is one append-only ledger row and one `inventory.*` event, written in the same transaction as the change. Issuers grant only within their namespace; people see and equip what they own. Live's name effects, particles, hats and voices are the first kinds, and `scripts/import-live.js` moves Live's unlocks and equipped slots here. A Workshop lets a signed-in person make community badges.

## What it does not do yet

Nothing is sold, bought, traded or converted into OpenCoins or Vibes, and there are no paid random rewards. Since 2026-10-09 [[OpenVibe.Live]] reads and writes cosmetics through Inventory, and [[OpenVibe.Games]] grants items for achievements. Creator submissions and staff review come later.
## How it fits the network

Identity is [[OpenVibe.Network]]'s; files are [[OpenVibe.Media]]'s; event delivery is [[OpenVibe.Events]]'. Live's cosmetics tables stay [[OpenVibe.Live]]'s, and Live's grantors include [[OpenVibe.Quest]].

## Status

It runs on Node 22 and Express with PostgreSQL and Valkey, on port 5030, and is licensed AGPL-3.0.

pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Play** keeps the achievements, leaderboards and cloud saves of every OpenVibe game at `play.openvibe.network`.

## What it does

- **Titles.** A game registers a title with its own Network token. Only that game writes to the title.
- **Achievements.** A title defines its achievements, including hidden ones. Unlocks are idempotent.
- **Leaderboards.** A board ranks each player's best score or the sum of their scores, this week or all time. Score posts are idempotent by round, so a retry never counts twice.
- **Cloud saves.** Up to 8 save slots per player per game, each any JSON up to 64 KB, versioned so two devices never overwrite each other silently; `openvibe-sdk/play` reads and writes them.
- **Guests.** A guest's progress becomes the person's when the game adopts them after they sign in.
- **Merged accounts.** When two OpenVibe accounts merge, their rows merge too.
- **Reads.** The boards and titles are public, as pages and JSON. Each signed-in person sees their own achievements across games.

## How it fits the network

- [[OpenVibe.Games]] is its first title owner, posting from its own tables.
- Sign-in and app tokens come from [[OpenVibe.Network]].
- People's rows are part of the account export and are erased with the account.

## Status

STATUS.json's stage is "alpha"; it is deployed on the network's host.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Zone
pages.summary: Private S3-compatible storage zones for OpenVibe projects at openvibe.zone: named buckets per project environment, scoped access keys and quotas, with the objects kept by OpenVibe.Media.
pages.body:
**OpenVibe.Zone** gives every OpenVibe project private storage zones at `openvibe.zone`. A zone is an S3 bucket of one project environment, sandbox or production.

## What it does

- **Default zones.** Each environment has a default zone, which holds its existing objects.
- **Named zones.** A project creates more zones by name, each with an optional quota.
- **Names are never reused.** A zone's name is never given to another zone, even after it is deleted, so a URL signed for one bucket can never reach a different one.
- **Access keys** read, write or both. A key can be limited to some zones, and its secret is shown once.
- **S3 tools.** The AWS SDKs, rclone and backup tools reach zones over S3, path style.
- **Large files and copies.** Multipart uploads carry big objects in parts, and server-side copies (CopyObject and UploadPartCopy) move data between zones without downloading it.
- **Usage.** Requests, egress and stored bytes are counted per zone by the hour. The console shows each zone's month so far, and the project's usage page adds them up.
- **Deletion.** Deleting a zone removes every object and every copy of it. A zone holding an object under a retention hold cannot be deleted.

## How it fits the network

- **Zone owns** the zone records and their control API.
- **[[OpenVibe.Media]] owns** what is inside a zone: the objects, their bytes and copies, the S3 surface, the access keys, quota enforcement and the one deletion path. Every object in a zone is an ordinary Media object, reachable through Media's own API too.
- Projects and roles come from [[OpenVibe.Network]].
- [[OpenVibe.Services]] lists zones beside a project's other resources and can delete one.

## Status

STATUS.json's stage is "alpha". Multipart uploads, server-side copies and per-zone usage were added on 2026-10-15. The S3 endpoint is `s3.openvibe.network` until `s3.openvibe.media` has its DNS record.

pages.title: OpenVibe.Node
pages.summary: One service for a person's computers, servers, Raspberry Pis, phones and robots: pair it once and OpenVibe.Bot and OpenVibe.Actor can use the device, with a local kill switch.
pages.body:
**OpenVibe Node** runs on a person's own devices: computers, servers, Raspberry Pis, phones and robots. Paired once with OpenVibe, it lets products such as [[OpenVibe.Bot]] and [[OpenVibe.Actor]] use the device.

## What it does

- **The core** is one static Go binary per platform.
  - It connects out over one WebSocket and needs no open ports.
  - It keeps heartbeats, a deadman and a persisted emergency stop, and owner limits are clamped before any driver sees a value.
  - It publishes video over WHIP.
  - It installs as a system service on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- **Plugins** run as separate processes: robot drivers (Adeept, Cozmo, ROS 2, and the community's LOOI driver) and the computer plugin. Every plugin stops its own actuators when its link goes quiet.
- **The computer plugin** lets an AI agent work on the machine only at the level its owner sets:
  - reading the screen;
  - files;
  - a terminal;
  - the mouse and keyboard;
  - a browser of the agent's own, in its own profile.

  At the "ask" level, each action waits for the owner's approval on the machine. The owner can answer from the tray
  (`openvibe-node tray`, on Linux and Windows), from a notification's Approve and Deny buttons, from a dialog on macOS,
  or from the command line. An approval is not taken while the agent itself is using the mouse or keyboard.
- **The local kill switch** (`openvibe-node stop`) stops every motor and keeps it stopped.

## How it fits the network

Devices pair through [[OpenVibe.Network]] or [[OpenVibe.Bot]]. Bot drives robots through it, and [[OpenVibe.Actor]] uses its computer plugin for computer control.

## Status

Released as versioned binaries. Mouse and keyboard input arrived in v0.9.0, the browser in v0.10.0, and approvals from the desktop in v0.11.0.
